topIssues.title: cci-stats: job lists are silently truncated at CircleCI's page size
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
`fetchJobs` in `cci-stats/pkg/service/service.go` calls
`client.Workflows.ListWorkflowJobs(ctx, id)` and uses the returned items without
following `NextPageToken`, so any workflow with more jobs than CircleCI's page
size has been recorded with only the first page. Test results for the missing
jobs are absent too.

This is not fixable in place: `ListWorkflowJobs(ctx context.Context, id string)`
in `github.com/axelKingsley/go-circleci` takes no options argument, so there is
nowhere to pass a page token. The sibling `Pipelines.ListWorkflows` does accept
one and is now paginated correctly.

Options:

- patch or fork go-circleci to add an options argument
- call the endpoint directly for this one request
- replace the client

Long standing rather than new, and only bites above the page size. The monorepo's
largest workflow is around 34 jobs, so it may never have been hit — worth
confirming against the API before deciding how much to spend on it.

topPRs.title: cci-stats: Retry pipelines that were still running when indexed
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
`processPipeline` wrote nothing for a pipeline that still had a workflow running.
The ingest high water mark is `MAX(created_at)` over `pipelines`, and pipelines do
not finish in creation order, so a later pipeline pushed the mark past the skipped
one and it was never revisited. Those pipelines are lost permanently.

Record unfinished pipelines with `complete = FALSE` instead, so the mark can
advance safely, and reindex them each run until done. Only terminal workflows
contribute jobs and test results, so one slow workflow no longer discards the data
for the rest of its pipeline. Newly listed pipelines are claimed as incomplete
before indexing starts, so a run that stops part way does not strand them either.

A pipeline is complete once it will create no more workflows — state `errored`, or
`created` with at least one workflow — and every matched workflow is terminal. The
state check matters because dynamic config generation creates the real workflows
via the continuation request, and setup reporting success is not ordered against
that; measured over 20 pipelines the gap ran from -1s to +2s. Judging on the
workflow list alone writes a pipeline off a second before its workflows appear.

Retries are bounded by `FETCH_LIMIT_DAYS`, and a retried pipeline that cannot be
fetched is skipped rather than failing the run, since it would otherwise recur
every run and block all indexing until it ages out. Reindexing never clears a
job's stored test results unless it has new ones to put back, because a spurious
not found is indistinguishable from a job with no tests.

See "Reading the data" in the README for two changes that affect queries:
`pipelines` now has rows with no `jobs` children, and `jobs.status` now includes
`canceled` / `not_run` / `unauthorized`.

**Prerequisite:** apply `pkg/db/migrate_v1_to_v2.sql` before this deploys. Draft
until then.

## Testing

Build, vet, `gofmt` and tests pass. `pkg/service/report_test.go` drives
`GenerateReport` against fakes for the client's four interfaces and covers the
cycle end to end, plus each failure mode this PR addresses: results surviving an
empty metadata fetch, a stuck retry not blocking other pipelines, every listed
pipeline getting a row, and the workflow list being followed across pages. Each
was checked to fail with its fix removed.

Two gaps remain. `pkg/db` has no tests, so the new query and both upserts are
unverified against real Postgres and there is no harness here to add one against.
And the non-`created` pipeline states come from CircleCI's OpenAPI spec and
documented transition flow rather than observation — all 300 pipelines I sampled
read `created`. The timing measurements above are direct observations.

`fetchJobs` still cannot paginate, because the client's `ListWorkflowJobs` takes
no options argument. Pre-existing and now documented: #710.

topPRs.title: cci-stats: Apply the schema with goose instead of by hand
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
The schema was two hand-maintained files: `db.sql` for a new database, and a separate
script for an existing one. Nothing kept them in step, so a database built from scratch
and one carried forward could drift apart, and nothing recorded which version a database
was at — `schema_version` existed but no code read it, so a database behind the binary
failed part way through a run.

The schema is now the migration chain in `pkg/db/migrations`, embedded in the binary and
applied at startup under a Postgres advisory lock. Startup also stops when the database is
ahead of the binary, which a rolled-back deploy would otherwise leave unnoticed.

`00001_initial_schema.sql` is a baseline. It reproduces the schema applied by hand up to
now and is written to be a no-op against a database that already has it, so the deployed
database is adopted rather than rebuilt. `schema_version` is kept, unread, only so the two
paths produce the same schema; dropping it is a sensible follow-up.

No new migration here — this is the framework only.

**`DATABASE_URI` now needs a role with DDL rights.**

## Testing

`pkg/db` had no tests. It now has four, against the Postgres the `go-test` job already
runs, so no CI change was needed: a database built from nothing, a repeat run, adoption of
the hand-applied schema, and the refusal to run against a newer one. The adoption test
compares the adopted schema against a freshly built one column by column and index by
index, so the two paths cannot diverge unnoticed.

The tests skip when no database is reachable, but fail instead when `CI` is set, so a
missing database cannot pass silently.

I could not run them locally — this environment has no Postgres and no container runtime —
so CI is their first real execution. `gofmt`, `go vet` and `go build` are clean, and the
service tests pass. `golangci-lint` is not installed here either, so lint is CI's first run
too.

### @​babel/core: Arbitrary File Read via sourceMappingURL Comment
[CVE-2026-49356](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-49356) / [GHSA-4x5r-pxfx-6jf8](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-4x5r-pxfx-6jf8)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact

Using `@babel/core` to compile maliciously crafted code can allow ab attacker to read any source map from the system that is running Babel, if these conditions are _all_ true:
- the attacker controls the input source code
- the attacker can read the output source code
- the attacker knows the path of the source map file that they want to read

**Users that only compile trusted code are not impacted.**

##### Patches

The vulnerability has been fixed in `@babel/core@7.29.6` and `@babel/core@8.0.0-rc.6`.

##### Workarounds

Callers can mitigate the issue without upgrading by setting [`inputSourceMap: false`](https://babeljs.io/docs/options#inputsourcemap) in their Babel options.

Callers can also manually extract the `#sourceMappingURL` comment from the input source code, validate whether the source map that it links to is allowed to be read, and if it is pass an object to `inputSourceMap` (passing `false` when it's not).

##### Credits

Thanks Teodor-Cristian Radoi for reporting the vulnerability.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 3.2 / 10 (Low)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:L/I:N/A:N`

---

### Fix transparency log tile verification bypass in golang.org/x/mod/sumdb/tlog
[CVE-2026-56865](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-56865) / [GO-2026-6179](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6179)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
A malicious GOPROXY was previously capable of forging up to two sumdb tiles that allow for a requested module to bypass the GOSUMDB check and persist attacker-controlled module content to a local Go module cache.

This attack allows for a malicious GOPROXY to serve malicious module content that cannot be detected by evaluating the transparency log.

All tiles are now correctly verified against their parents.

In order to determine if you have been affected:

rm -r go.sum go.work.sum vendor/ && go mod tidy

#### Severity
Unknown

#### References
- [https://go.dev/issue/80744](https://go.dev/issue/80744)
- [https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/94pEornpRlI](https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/94pEornpRlI)
- [https://go.dev/cl/814960](https://go.dev/cl/814960)
- [https://go.dev/cl/815020](https://go.dev/cl/815020)

</details>

### Ignore unrelated, unauthenticated hashes in Lookup in golang.org/x/mod/sumdb
[CVE-2026-56864](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-56864) / [GO-2026-6180](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6180)

<details>
